maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: None. The class the advisory names cannot be loaded, because it is not on the classpath of any Vaadin application.

maven-io-netty-netty-codec-http-2026.impact: None for a production application without Control Center that makes no reactor-netty calls of its own. Otherwise the code handles traffic with the servers your own client calls, or with your Kubernetes API server.
maven-io-netty-netty-codec-http-2026.workaround: Set <netty.version>4.1.139.Final</netty.version> in the pom that inherits spring-boot-starter-parent. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26, 24.7.17, 24.9.24 and 24.10.12: it moves every io.netty artifact to 4.1.139.Final, which osv.dev lists clean. That measures resolution, not compatibility, so run your tests. If your pom only imports spring-boot-dependencies, the property does nothing and you manage the io.netty artifacts in your own dependencyManagement instead, which was not measured here.
maven-io-netty-netty-codec-http-2026.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. No free Spring Boot release a Vaadin 24 line declares pins a fixed netty: 3.2.12, 3.4.13 and 3.5.16, the newest of their lines on 2026-10-24, pin 4.1.115.Final, 4.1.130.Final and 4.1.135.Final. It arrives when Spring Boot raises netty.version; until then, the property.

maven-org-apache-logging-log4j-log4j-api.impact: None. The artifacts the two advisories are about are not resolved by the application.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None through Vaadin or Spring on the 24 series. Your own code that parses a DataInput with Jackson is a separate question.
maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.workaround: None needed, unless your own code parses a java.io.DataInput with Jackson.

maven-org-jsoup-jsoup-cleaner-and-xml.impact: None through Vaadin. Two things are affected and both are your own code rather than ours, cleaning untrusted HTML with a safelist you built that permits a raw text element, and parsing untrusted XML with jsoup.

maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.impact: None unless request input reaches the API each one needs: a path pattern handed to AntPathMatcher, a SpEL expression built from input, data binding of user supplied property paths, field errors rendered through Errors.getFieldErrors(), functional endpoint SSE, or a Content-Disposition built from an untrusted file name.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.workaround: On 24.7, <spring-framework.version>6.2.19</spring-framework.version> clears CVE-2026-41848; on 24.4 the same property resolves and clears it too, but moves Spring Boot 3.2 onto a Spring Framework minor it was not built for, so test it first. The fixes for the other six exist only in Broadcom's commercial releases, so nothing you can download clears them on any 24 series.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.fix_expected: The releases that fix these, spring-core 6.1.29 and 6.2.20, are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support, and the 2026-11-19 Spring cycle moved that stream on to 6.1.30, 6.2.21 and Spring Boot 3.5.18: Maven Central still ends the free lines at 6.1.21, 6.2.19 and Spring Boot 3.5.16 and answers 404 for all three of the newer ones, read on 2026-11-20.

maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.impact: None from Vaadin. For an application that renders XsltView under a /** mapping, CVE-2026-47884 is remote code execution: the verdict is that Vaadin does not create the condition, not that the condition is harmless.
maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.workaround: If you render XSLT views, name the view explicitly rather than letting the mapping derive it from the request path. Raising the Spring Framework version from your pom does not help: the 6.1 and 6.2 releases that carry the fix exist only under Broadcom's commercial Spring support.
maven-org-springframework-spring-webmvc-.fix_expected: Fixed publicly only in Spring Framework 7.0.9, which needs Spring Boot 4 and so Vaadin 25. spring.io marks 6.2.20 and 6.1.29 Enterprise Support Only.

npm-opentelemetry-core.impact: None without an application that extracts baggage headers from incoming requests.

javascript-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-.impact: None through the Markdown component. If your own code calls DOMPurify with those options, it is exposed as each advisory describes.
javascript-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-.workaround: If your code calls DOMPurify, do not use those option combinations while your build bundles 3.4.16.
javascript-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-.fix_expected: Upstream 3.4.17 fixes all three. Your build moves to it when a Vaadin release moves the dompurify pin in @vaadin/bundles, as described in npm-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-10-23.

That measures resolution, not compatibility, so run your tests. If your pom only imports spring-boot-dependencies, the property does nothing and you manage the io.netty artifacts in your own dependencyManagement instead, which was not measured here.
maven-io-netty-family-not-reached.fix_expected: Spring Boot decides this version, not Vaadin. No free Spring Boot release a Vaadin 24 line declares pins a fixed netty: 3.2.12, 3.4.13 and 3.5.16, the newest of their lines on 2026-10-24, pin 4.1.115.Final, 4.1.130.Final and 4.1.135.Final. It arrives when Spring Boot raises netty.version; until then, the property.

maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.impact: None unless a Vaadin 24 application declares observability-kit-starter and whoever can send a baggage header can reach it. There it is a denial of service through memory and CPU, not a way in.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.workaround: With Spring Boot, set <opentelemetry.version>1.62.0</opentelemetry.version> in your pom; take it out once your Spring Boot pins 1.62.0 or later. Without Spring Boot that property moves nothing, because only Spring Boot's dependency management reads it: import io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-bom 1.62.0 in dependencyManagement. Do not declare observability-kit-starter 3.2.1 yourself on 24.4 or 24.7: since 3.2.0 its license listener extends a Flow class that first ships in flow-server 24.9, the listener is a registered service init listener, and the application fails at startup with NoClassDefFoundError. In every case resolution was measured, not compatibility with Observability Kit. If you do not use baggage, otel.propagators=tracecontext drops the baggage propagator instead. These moves change the jar your application resolves and not the copy inside the Observability Kit agent, which carries its own: the 3.2.1 and 4.1.2 agents carry OpenTelemetry 1.62.0 and 1.65.0, both past this one, and the 3.0.0 and 3.1.0 agents carry 1.23.0 and 1.44.1, which are not.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.fix_expected: With Spring Boot, on 24.4 and 24.7 none from any Spring Boot you can download: Maven Central ends those lines at 3.2.12 and 3.4.13, which pin 1.31.0 and 1.43.0, and later releases are published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support. On 24.9 and 24.10 a Spring Boot 3.5 patch pinning 1.62.0, which does not exist yet: 3.5.16, the newest open one, pins 1.49.0. Without Spring Boot, 24.9 and 24.10 already resolve 1.62.0 through Observability Kit 3.2.1 and need nothing, and on 24.4 and 24.7 the exit is an Observability Kit release built for those lines, a 3.1.1 from the 3.1.0 tag carrying a fixed OpenTelemetry, and a platform release pinning it on both branches. Kit 3.2.1 and later cannot be that release: they fail at startup on any Flow before 24.9.

maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.impact: None unless the application runs Commons Text or Commons Configuration interpolation over untrusted input. There a long class name stops the thread with an Error that most code does not catch.
maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.workaround: With spring-boot-starter-parent, set <commons-lang3.version>3.18.0</commons-lang3.version> in the properties of your pom. Without that parent, declare org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 3.18.0 in your dependencyManagement. Measured on 2026-10-24 on Spring Boot 3.5.16: the property moves 24.9.24 and 24.10.12 from 3.17.0 to 3.18.0. That measures resolution, not compatibility.
maven-org-apache-commons-commons-lang3-c.fix_expected: No Spring Boot 3.5 release carries it: the newest, 3.5.16, pins 3.17.0.

maven-io-netty-netty-transport-2026-10-2.impact: None through netty-transport. Read the findings on the artifact each advisory actually names, in particular netty-codec-http and netty-handler, which a Vaadin 24 application does resolve and which carry real advisories at these versions.

maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.impact: None unless the application registers UrlHandlerFilter with very broad patterns, or maps UrlFilenameViewController with an end of path pattern and no prefix. There a crafted link redirects to another site.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.workaround: If you register UrlHandlerFilter, give it narrow patterns; if you map UrlFilenameViewController, configure a prefix. The 6.2 release that fixes either, 6.2.20, is commercial from Broadcom, so raising the version from your pom cannot reach it.
maven-org-springframework-spring-core-24.fix_expected: Fixed on Maven Central only in Spring Framework 7.0.9, which needs Spring Boot 4 and so Vaadin 25. The 6.2 fix, 6.2.20, is published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support, where the 2026-11-19 Spring cycle added 6.2.21; Maven Central still ends 6.2 at 6.2.19 and answers 404 for both, read on 2026-11-20.

maven-io-netty-netty-codec-memcache-2026.impact: None through netty-codec-memcache. Read the findings on the artifact each advisory actually names, in particular netty-codec-http and netty-handler, which a Vaadin 24 application does resolve and which carry real advisories at these versions.

npm-minimatch-globparts-24.impact: None unless your own build code passes a glob pattern that someone outside your team can choose to glob or minimatch. There, a crafted pattern makes the build spend excessive CPU and memory.

maven-io-vertx-vertx-web-client-cpe-2026.impact: None through vertx-web-client. Each of these is about a Vert.x module your application does not resolve.

maven-io-vertx-vertx-core-websocket-2026.impact: None for a deployed Vaadin application, with or without Control Center. An application without Control Center does not resolve Vert.x at all.
maven-io-vertx-vertx-core-websocket-2026.workaround: None needed. If your policy forbids the jar at an affected version, pin io.vertx:vertx-core to 4.5.35, which Maven Central carries (checked 2026-10-24); not measured against a Control Center deployment.
maven-io-vertx-vertx-core-websocket-2026.fix_expected: No Vaadin release will carry it: Control Center is no longer developed, so the version it pins stays at 4.5.34. 4.5.35 is upstream for anyone who wants it.

maven-io-vertx-vertx-core-cpe-2026-10-22.impact: None through vertx-core. Each of these is about a Vert.x module your application does not resolve.

npm-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-10-23.impact: None through the Markdown component. Code of your own that calls DOMPurify with those options is exposed as each advisory describes.
npm-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-10-23.workaround: If your code calls DOMPurify, do not use those option combinations while your tree resolves 3.4.16.
npm-dompurify-markdown-24-9-2026-10-23.fix_expected: Upstream 3.4.17 clears all three. @vaadin/bundles 24.9.20 and 24.10.8 declare dompurify 3.4.16 exactly as a peer dependency, and the scans of 24.9.25 and 24.10.13 resolve 3.4.16, so it moves when a Vaadin release moves that pin.

maven-org-codehaus-plexus-plexus-utils-2.impact: None. The vulnerable method is present and nothing in the application or the build calls it.
maven-org-codehaus-plexus-plexus-utils-2.fix_expected: Merged into flow main on 2026-10-07. It is not in a Vaadin release yet.

maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.impact: None unless the application builds its own token service on KeyBasedPersistenceTokenService. There an attacker who can submit tokens repeatedly learns the expected value one character at a time from how long each rejection takes.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.workaround: If your code declares a KeyBasedPersistenceTokenService, compare the token yourself with java.security.MessageDigest.isEqual, which does not return early. There is no property to set.
maven-org-springframework-security-sprin.fix_expected: No free release for Vaadin 24. Maven Central ends 6.4 at 6.4.13 and 6.5 at 6.5.11, both in range, and the open source fixes, 7.0.7 and 7.1.1, need Spring Boot 4. Setting spring-security.version to 6.5.11 on 24.7 does not change this.

maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.impact: Every Vaadin 24.9 and 24.10 application on the embedded Tomcat. Most of the ten need a Tomcat feature a Spring Boot application does not configure by default (FORM or DIGEST authentication, DataSourceRealm, security-role-ref, the rewrite valve, unix domain sockets); CVE-2026-73180 is about WebSocket sessions outliving the HTTP session, and Vaadin push uses WebSocket.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.workaround: Add <tomcat.version>10.1.62</tomcat.version> to the properties of your pom; 10.1.61, recommended here until 2026-11-20, is inside the ranges of the ten advisories Tomcat published on 2026-11-19, which have their own verdict, and 10.1.62 clears both sets. Measured on 2026-11-20 on 24.10.14 with Spring Boot 3.5.16 and on 24.7.19 with 3.4.13: tomcat-embed-core, tomcat-embed-el and tomcat-embed-websocket move to 10.1.62. Only resolution was measured, not a running application. Remove it once your Spring Boot pins a fixed Tomcat.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.fix_expected: A Spring Boot 3.5 patch that pins Tomcat 10.1.59 or later, and then a 24.9 or 24.10 release that declares it. Neither is published as of 2026-11-20, when Maven Central still ends Spring Boot 3.5 at 3.5.16 and answers 404 for the 3.5.18 of the 2026-11-19 Spring cycle, which is commercial only.

javascript-dompurify-quill-cpe-2021-3163.impact: None from DOMPurify, which this advisory does not describe. The Quill code in the same file is covered by the verdict npm-quill-2021-3163.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None unless your application binds JSON from the browser to a float, double, BigDecimal or Number through Jackson: a Hilla endpoint or signal, a ReactAdapterComponent of your own, or your own REST controller. There, a crafted number sent as a string makes the request spend excessive CPU.
maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.workaround: Set <jackson-bom.version>2.21.7</jackson-bom.version> in the properties of your own pom, and take it out once your Spring Boot pins a fixed Jackson itself.
maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.fix_expected: A Spring Boot 3.5 release that pins Jackson 2.21.7. Maven Central has none as of 2026-11-02, and no Vaadin release moves this version.

maven-org-springframework-spring-core-cp.impact: None through spring-core. If you add Spring WebFlux, RSocket or FreeMarker yourself, read these on that code.

maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.impact: None unless the application sets management.endpoint.env.post.enabled=true and exposes the env endpoint over HTTP. Where both are true, whoever reaches the endpoint sets any property they like.
maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.workaround: Leave management.endpoint.env.post.enabled unset and keep env out of management.endpoints.web.exposure.include. The 4.3 release carrying the fix, 4.3.4, is commercial from Broadcom and not on Maven Central.
maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.fix_expected: The advisory fixes the 4.3 line in 4.3.4, which is published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support and not on Maven Central, whose 4.3 metadata ended at 4.3.3 when read on 2026-10-24.

npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.impact: None in a deployed application. On a developer machine, two of the launch-editor advisories need Windows and the third needs an editor such as Vim or Emacs and a file named with a leading plus or minus sign.
npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.workaround: Upgrade within your line where a release carries the fix: 24.10.12 resolves vite 7.3.7, 25.2.12 and 25.3.3 resolve 8.3.4. An overrides entry for launch-editor changes nothing, because vite compiles it into its own files.
npm-vite-dev-server-2026-10-22.fix_expected: Not on 23.6, 24.4, 24.7 or 24.9 yet. Vaadin names vite exactly, so a rebuilt lockfile never takes a fix on its own: 24.9.24 still pins 7.3.6 and 24.7.17 pins 6.4.3, one patch below 7.3.7 and 6.4.4, published 2026-10-06, and the 3.2 and 5.4 lines that 23.6 and 24.4 pin have no fixed release.

maven-io-projectreactor-netty-reactor-ne.impact: None. No Reactor Netty server is ever created, so nothing listens for the requests the advisory describes.

npm-glob-abort-signal-24.impact: None unless your own build code passes an AbortSignal to glob to limit a walk. There, the walk keeps reading the file system after it was cancelled.

maven-org-jetbrains-kotlin-kotlin-stdlib.impact: None. Nothing in the application calls the two deprecated functions.

maven-io-opentelemetry-family-2026-10-22.impact: None. These advisories are about the Go and JavaScript implementations of OpenTelemetry, not the Java libraries your application resolves.

maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.impact: None unless one of your own types bound from browser JSON uses one of those features, or copilot runs in production. Where it does, the advisory is a denial of service, a property set that should have been ignored, or a lookup the server should not make.
maven-com-fasterxml-jackson-core-jackson.workaround: If one of your types meets a condition above, set <jackson-bom.version>2.18.12</jackson-bom.version> on 24.4 and 24.7, or <jackson-bom.version>2.21.7</jackson-bom.version> on 24.9 and 24.10, in the properties of your own pom. These are the properties the jackson-databind risk verdicts for those series carry, measured on 2026-10-24.

maven-me-friwi-jcef-api.impact: None. The CEF your application resolves is newer than the fix.

maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.impact: None unless the application runs an Observability Kit agent older than 3.2.2, or code of its own extracts trace context from incoming requests. There anybody who can send a request can make each one cost CPU through a crafted tracestate header, a denial of service and not a way in.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.workaround: Update the agent to observability-kit-agent 3.2.2 from Maven Central; it is the jar the JVM is started with, so no application rebuild is involved. Until then, cap or remove the tracestate header at your proxy or load balancer before requests reach the application, or start the agent with -Dotel.propagators=none if you do not need trace context from upstream callers. Raising opentelemetry.version in your pom moves the jar your scanner reports and does not change the agent.
maven-io-opentelemetry-opentelemetry-api.fix_expected: The observability-kit-agent 3.2.2 on Maven Central, published on 2026-11-11, built on the upstream Java agent 2.33.1, whose shaded parser scans the header instead of compiling a pattern for it.

maven-com-vaadin-vaadin-swing-kit-flow.impact: None. The advisory is about flow-server of Vaadin 19 and earlier, not about Swing Kit.

maven-org-jetbrains-kotlin-kotlin-stdlib.impact: None. The affected code is build tooling and is not in this library.

maven-org-apache-logging-log4j-log4j-api.impact: None as a Vaadin application is put together. With Log4j 2 as the backend and the JSON template layout, a log entry carrying NaN or Infinity becomes a document a conformant parser refuses, which breaks log collection rather than the application.
maven-org-apache-logging-log4j-log4j-api.workaround: Add <log4j2.version>2.25.5</log4j2.version> to the properties of your pom if you want the finding gone. Measured on 2026-10-24 on 24.4.26, 24.7.17, 24.9.24 and 24.10.12, each with the Spring Boot it declares: log4j-api and log4j-to-slf4j move to 2.25.5, from 2.21.1 on 24.4 and from 2.24.3 on the others. Only resolution was measured, not a running application.
maven-org-apache-logging-log4j-log4j-api.fix_expected: None published: Spring Boot 3.2.12, 3.4.13 and 3.5.16, the newest of the lines these series use, pin Log4j 2.21.1, 2.24.3 and 2.24.3.

maven-io-netty-netty-codec-mqtt-2026-10-.impact: None through netty-codec-mqtt. Read the findings on the artifact each advisory actually names, in particular netty-codec-http and netty-handler, which a Vaadin 24 application does resolve and which carry real advisories at these versions.

Only resolution was measured, not a running application. Remove it once your Spring Boot pins a fixed Tomcat.
maven-org-apache-tomcat-embed-tomcat-emb.fix_expected: A Spring Boot 3.5 patch that pins Tomcat 10.1.57 or later, and then a 24.9 or 24.10 release that declares it. Neither is published as of 2026-11-20, when Maven Central still ends Spring Boot 3.5 at 3.5.16 and answers 404 for the 3.5.18 of the 2026-11-19 Spring cycle, which is commercial only.

maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.impact: None unless the application sets management.endpoint.env.post.enabled=true and exposes the env endpoint over HTTP. Where both are true, whoever reaches the endpoint sets any property they like.
maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.workaround: Leave management.endpoint.env.post.enabled unset and keep env out of management.endpoints.web.exposure.include. The 4.3 release carrying the fix, 4.3.4, is commercial from Broadcom and not on Maven Central.
maven-org-springframework-cloud-spring-c.fix_expected: The advisory fixes the 4.3 line in 4.3.4, which is published by Broadcom under commercial Spring support and not on Maven Central, whose 4.3 metadata ended at 4.3.3 when read on 2026-10-24.

javascript-quill-dompurify-advisories.impact: None from Quill, which these advisories do not describe. The DOMPurify code in the same file is covered by the verdict javascript-dompurify-markdown-24-9.

npm-quill-2021-3163.impact: None through RichTextEditor.setValue or the editor itself, which clean the HTML. HTML that reaches the editor in the browser without that cleaning can run script in the browser of whoever views it.
npm-quill-2021-3163.workaround: Nothing, if HTML reaches the editor only through RichTextEditor.setValue or what users type. If your code calls dangerouslySetHtmlValue or feeds the element from client code, pass the HTML through RichTextEditor.setValue instead, or clean it with jsoup first.
npm-quill-2021-3163.fix_expected: None upstream: GHSA-4943-9vgg-gr5r says no patch exists and no further Quill 1 releases are planned.
